replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed threats against this design:

- Automated abuse (brute force, mass sign-up, email/SMS flooding, scraping): design describes only "Customers can request account deletion. Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." — no sign-in, form, messaging or listing endpoint is stated. Not present in design.
- Staff/admin screens rendering user-supplied content: no support UI, comment, file or profile field is described ("fileUpload":false). Not present in design.
- Privileged action with no record of who did it: present — "Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." Already covered by listed threat 5 (no record of who requested or performed a deletion).
- Cacheable personal/account documents or pages: no document, export or page delivery is described. Not present in design.
- Attacker-controlled text flowing into logs, CSV/exports, emails or another interpreter: "logs" appear only as retained copies ("Copies in the warehouse, logs and backups are left as is"); no export, email or header rendering is stated. Not present in design.
- Unconfirmed #1 (flag cleared / restored): same weakness and harm as listed threat 4. Not a gap.
- Unconfirmed #2 (sessions/tokens not revoked on deletion): the design states deletion is only "marks the account as deleted in the main database", so continued authenticated access after deletion is a different attack and harm from data remnants in warehouse/backups. Not covered.
- Unconfirmed #3 (code paths ignoring the flag): depends on how queries are built and is a consequence of the retained-record threats already listed. Not a gap.

  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["support deletion action", "main database", "warehouse", "log pipeline", "backups"],
    "dataStores": ["main database", "warehouse", "logs", "backups"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["customer -> support", "support -> main database"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Deleted accounts keep working because deletion is only a database flag",
      "scenario": "Deletion consists only of support marking the account as deleted in the main database. Nothing in the design ends the account's live access. A customer who asked for deletion, or an attacker who already holds that customer's session or API credential, keeps using the product as that account after the deletion is actioned: reading and changing the customer's data and generating new activity for an account the business and the customer both believe is gone. The customer's deletion request is not honoured in practice, and the continued activity is attributed to a closed account.",
      "component": "Support deletion action / main database account flag",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers can request account deletion. Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V3.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "Marking an account deleted in the database doesn't log it out, so whoever holds its existing login can keep using it after deletion.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Revoke all access when an account is marked deleted",
        "given": "a customer account that support marks as deleted in the main database",
        "when": "the deletion is actioned",
        "then": "all sessions, tokens and API credentials for that account are invalidated immediately and any subsequent authenticated request with them is rejected"
      }
    }
  ]
}
